title: Resume a sorted vCenter privilege inventory after token expiry
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a complete, reproducible vCenter authorization-privilege inventory even when the access token on its authenticated SDK handle expires on a continuation page. Complete `VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventory/VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventory.psm1` so the current page is retried after one refresh without discarding any earlier page.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is the wire authority. The only vSphere Automation operationId in scope is exactly `Vcenter.Authorization.Privileges_list`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.vSphere` version `13.5.0.25380678`. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file. In the production path, lazily import that genuine module and use `Initialize-VcenterAuthorizationPrivilegesIterationSpec` and `Invoke-VcenterAuthorizationPrivilegesList`. Do not bypass the SDK with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, raw sockets, or a subprocess.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these commands:

- `New-VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventorySession -Server <object> -RefreshConnection <scriptblock> [-OperationInvoker <scriptblock>]` returns a new independent session and performs no request. `Server` is the caller-owned authenticated vSphere SDK server handle. `RefreshConnection` receives the expired handle and must return a newly authenticated handle. `OperationInvoker` is the protected verifier seam; when omitted, dispatch through the two generated VCF PowerCLI cmdlets named above.
- `Get-VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventory -Session <object> [-PageSize <int64>]` retrieves every page. `PageSize` defaults to the specification default of 200 and must be positive.

For every page create an iteration spec with `page_size`. Omit `marker` on the first request; for a continuation request, pass the previous response marker exactly as returned. Do not pass a filter object and do not pass `is_on_parent`, `names`, or `versions`. Every unset optional value must remain absent rather than becoming null, false, zero, an empty string, an empty array, or an SDK default.

When the operation fails with HTTP 401, call `RefreshConnection` once for that exact failed request, atomically replace the session's server handle, and retry the identical operation parameters once. Preserve all previously collected pages. A second 401 for the retry is terminal. Do not refresh for another HTTP status, do not restart pagination, and do not include an access token, authentication-header value, expired handle rendering, response body, or nested transport message in a refresh-related error. Keep the replacement handle for later inventory calls.

Reject a null page, missing or null `Items`, a null item, a blank `Privilege`, missing `Info`, a blank `Info.Name`, a non-string marker, an empty marker, a non-empty marker paired with an empty page, or a repeated marker. Buffer results until all pages succeed. Return the complete list sorted by `Privilege` with `StringComparer.Ordinal`; do not trust server or page order.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier generates all tokens, markers, and privilege data at runtime, starts `mock_vcenter.py` on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its fsynced request log. The mock derives its only route from `docs/contract.json`, expires the first token on a continuation page, and flips collection element order on every successful response. Verification checks the exact GET target and query order, retry-target identity, `vmware-api-session-id` token transition, headers, empty body, marker continuity, preservation of the first page, complete ordinal sorting across repeated runs, replacement-handle reuse, and omission of every unset optional query field. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected; edit only `VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventory/VcfVcenterPrivilegeInventory.psm1`.
